speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me when the feeding difficulties and abdominal distension first started, and has the baby been vomiting or having trouble passing stool?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Doctor
text: Has the baby passed any stool or gas in the last 24 hours, and does the vomit, if present, appear green?

speaker: Patient
text: There has not been fever, vomiting, or diarrhea like a stomach infection. The baby was born at 39 weeks without birth complications.

speaker: Doctor
text: Has the baby passed any stool or gas at all since birth, and has a rectal exam revealed a tight anal sphincter or a sudden release of stool and gas upon withdrawal?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby did not seem to pass stool normally and the belly swelling has become more obvious. Feeding has clearly decreased over the past few days.

speaker: Doctor

REQUEST TEST: Abdominal X-Ray

Given the history of delayed stool passage and worsening distension, I need to check for a transition zone that might indicate Hirschsprung's disease.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Abdominal X-ray findings show dilated bowel segments with absence of gas in the rectum, suggesting a possible obstruction.

speaker: Patient

REQUEST TEST: Contrast Enema

The abdominal X-ray showing no significant finding is concerning given the clinical picture of delayed stool passage and distension, so I need to visualize the colon directly to rule out a transition zone or other obstruction.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Barium Enema findings show a transition zone in the distal colon, compatible with Hirschsprung disease.
